scams.name: Melbourne Airport Fake Taxi / DiDi Bait Scam
scams.tldr: This is Melbourne Airport's most-complained-about tourist scam in 2024–2026.
scams.description: This is Melbourne Airport's most-complained-about tourist scam in 2024–2026. A traveler report titled 'Taxi scam at melb airport' (1fi2uj2);coaxed' by a taxi tout into a $40-Uber ride becoming a six-figure taxi bill. Another thread 'Melbourne airport taxi/didi scam' (18y4qgb);they were probably banking on tourists to not check their credit card statements.' The traveler threads 'Just got charged $99 for a 15 min taxi ride' (1mg5207) has the memorable detail: 'As we were leaving the airport I realized he was covering the metre. I asked him to uncover it. It was already over $27, we had been driving five minutes.' traveler reports 1irx6v5 notes that Melbourne Airport itself has installed signs warning travelers about these 'taxi' drivers — the scam is now sophisticated enough that airport management is actively counter-messaging.
scams.avoidance: Ignore all in-terminal transport offers — walk outside to the signposted ranks and rideshare bays. Verify driver photo and license plate in the Uber/DiDi/Bolt app before entering the car. Take SkyBus ($22, runs every 10 min to Southern Cross Station) if in any doubt. Make the driver uncover the meter before pulling away — 'turn the meter on' is your first words. Pay with card on the in-car terminal for chargeback protection — never hand cash to an unmarked driver.
scams.location: Melbourne Airport (Tullamarine), T2 and T4 arrivals, and the prepaid taxi/rideshare rank

scams.name: SIXT / Budget Phantom Rental-Car Damage Claim
scams.tldr: SIXT Australia's phantom damage fee practice is the most-complained-about rental-car issue on traveler reports and traveler reports.
scams.description: SIXT Australia's phantom damage fee practice is the most-complained-about rental-car issue on traveler reports and traveler reports. traveler threads 'Australia SixT Rental Car Fraud' (1ijoe2f). traveler reports 'Excessive damage fee ($6.5k) from SIXT' (173e1wh) has one traveler hit with a $6,500 invoice for alleged underbody damage — 'it said that in the T&Cs they clearly outline' pattern that allows the charge. traveler reports 'Sixt Car Rental Damage Scam' (1cto8uk);Sixt Rental rush you through pickup, and when you ask about the preexisting damage or attempt to take photos they tell you Don't worry, it's all logged.' The damage is not logged; weeks later, a charge appears. This also happens with Budget, Thrifty and Hertz Australia at lower frequency, but SIXT is statistically the worst offender in 2024–2026 Reddit reports.
scams.avoidance: Film the entire car on video at both pickup AND drop-off — all sides, underneath, interior, dashboard. Insist on a signed no-damage receipt at drop-off with the desk agent present — photograph it. Pay with a credit card that provides primary CDW insurance (Amex Platinum, Chase Sapphire, Capital One Venture X). Decline rental-desk CDW upsells if your card covers it — keep the rental cost transparent. If hit with a phantom charge, file a chargeback immediately and complain to Consumer Affairs Victoria.
scams.location: Melbourne Airport and CBD rental pickup counters — SIXT is the most-reported, but not the only

scams.name: Fake QR-Code Parking Ticket Sticker Scam
scams.tldr: Fake-parking-ticket QR scams exploded across Victoria in 2024 and are still documented weekly.
scams.description: Fake-parking-ticket QR scams exploded across Victoria in 2024 and are still documented weekly. A traveler threads titled 'QR Codes put on car' (17lpka2) has drivers comparing fake stickers placed on their vehicles in CBD and inner suburbs. traveler reports 'Fake Parking Ticket Warning' (14bkid3) has a close-up photo: 'Eagle-eyed drivers have noticed scam tickets which have a council logo, a barcode and other information also printed on real council parking tickets.' The traveler threads 'QR code parking scam' (1hfo20b). Either variant achieves the same outcome: your card data goes to a clone site, the scammers use the card for small online purchases initially to test it, then drain the account.
scams.avoidance: Never scan a QR code on a parking ticket or meter — type melbourne.vic.gov.au manually. Pay for parking only through the PayStay or CellOPark app downloaded from your app store. If you find a 'ticket', verify it by calling City of Melbourne (03 9658 9658) before paying. Photograph any suspicious sticker and report to City of Melbourne rangers for removal. If you've entered card details into a suspicious page, call your bank immediately and reissue.
scams.location: CBD street-side parking, Southbank car parks, Carlton and Fitzroy metered zones

scams.name: Fake Short-Stay Rental / 'Airbnb' Scam
scams.tldr: This exact pattern cost a Canadian working-holiday traveler AUD $3,266 — documented in a traveler report titled 'I got scammed 3266.00 AUD from a fake Airbnb website in Australia' (eca96f).
scams.description: This exact pattern cost a Canadian working-holiday traveler AUD $3,266 — documented in a traveler report titled 'I got scammed 3266.00 AUD from a fake Airbnb website in Australia' (eca96f). traveler reports's 'AirBnB scam' thread (195zy5a) explains the source material: 'They get photos and other details from old real estate listings and use them to create a fake airbnb listing.' traveler reports 'Is this a rental scam? Too good to be true' (1him29v) and 'Looking for advice on a recent rental scam' (13iss3e) document the same pattern for new-to-Melbourne residents who are desperate for short-term accommodation while looking for a permanent place. ABC News reported in August 2024 that these fake listings are escalating across Booking.com and Airbnb simultaneously.
scams.avoidance: Book only through airbnb.com or booking.com via the app or a bookmarked URL. Never pay by bank transfer, wire or crypto — legitimate platforms always escrow. Reverse image-search the listing photos in Google Images before paying. Check the listing has reviews from multiple guests in the past 12 months. Ask for a live video call tour of the property — refusal is a hard no.
scams.location: CBD, Docklands, Southbank, St Kilda — high-turnover short-stay areas

scams.name: Flinders Street / CBD Tram Pickpocket & Tab Bait
scams.tldr: Melbourne has lower pickpocket rates than Sydney, Paris or Rome, but the specific hotspot is the Flinders Street Station / Federation Square interchange and the tourist tram routes (70, 75, 96).
scams.description: Melbourne has lower pickpocket rates than Sydney, Paris or Rome, but the specific hotspot is the Flinders Street Station / Federation Square interchange and the tourist tram routes (70, 75, 96). A traveler threads titled 'PSA: Southbank Pickpocket' (2fzo9k);s father being targeted walking from the back of Flinders Street Station. traveler reports 'Absolute long shot but any chance someone found a wallet on the 70 tram line' (1fqn1le). traveler reports 'Streets or areas around CBD to avoid' (1br3szs) calls out 'Elizabeth Street near the intersection with Flinders Street' as the dodgiest stretch at night. A stranger who bumps you is almost never genuine — they're testing your reaction to set up a lift in the next crowd pulse.
scams.avoidance: Keep phone and wallet in a zipped front pocket, not a back pocket — obvious but chronic offence. Carry a slim crossbody bag across your chest, not a backpack on your back, on trams 70/75/96. Scrutinise every bar bill before signing — dispute any extra items or surcharges immediately. Tap your own card — never hand it to the staff to 'process' at the till. Use contactless or Myki for trams so your phone doesn't come out in crowded zones.
scams.location: Flinders Street Station, Federation Square, trams 70/75/96, Elizabeth Street

scams.name: Great Ocean Road 'Day Tour' Fake Booking Scam
scams.tldr: Consumer Affairs Victoria and ScamWatch have flagged multiple variants of this pattern.
scams.description: Consumer Affairs Victoria and ScamWatch have flagged multiple variants of this pattern. A TravelVictoria blog post (travelvictoria.com.au);Holiday Great Ocean Road' (holidaygreatoceanroad.com) as a historic false-billing scam listed on ScamWatch — the site cloned legitimate operator branding and processed payments with no actual tour to deliver. Fake booking sites still circulate via Google Ads and Facebook Ads targeting Melbourne visitors searching for Great Ocean Road, Phillip Island penguin tours, and Yarra Valley winery day trips. The site looks real, the pricing is aggressive (~20–40% below Gray Line or Go West Tours), and the 'tour' simply never happens.
scams.avoidance: Book through Gray Line, Go West, Autopia Tours, Bunyip Tours, or a verified Viator/GetYourGuide listing. Verify the operator's ABN at abn.business.gov.au — legitimate tours are ABN-registered. Pay only by credit card for chargeback protection — never bank transfer or PayPal F&F. Read TripAdvisor reviews from the last 6 months specifically — a gap suggests a new/fake listing. If no bus arrives, call the operator's landline first, then dispute the charge with your bank.
scams.location: Online booking sites + Southern Cross Station pickup zone
